What model should I start with

Personally, I'd say give a High Grade (1/144 scale) kit a try. Since I stick to UC mobile suits, I'm a bit biased toward HGUC, but if you can find an HG kit you like, go with that.

  • Sites: double-edged sword, since the pricing will beat brick-and-mortar stores but inflated shipping costs can be a deal-breaker. I have used Hobby Search and Hobby Link Japan but I am in NA.
  • Cost: HG kits that are reasonably priced will probably run you from 12 to 26 AUD, by my estimation. You can check for local retailers to see how much they are marking up their kits, then decide if you'd save by going online. I like to support local stores when I can.
  • Tools: some of this can be improvised, such as using shears to clip pieces off the trees, emery boards from a beauty shop for filing/sanding/smoothing, a fine-point Sharpie pen for detailing. These can get you by while you save a little extra for your tools. You will definitely want some kind of hobby knife eventually, and if you are keen to paint, Bandai licenses out official paint markers which are already color-matched to their specifications. I think they come in packs but you may be able to get individual colors as well. I think most of the essential tools should run you less than 8 AUD, but I'm not certain.

Hope that helps. If you get up and running, you should follow up with pics of your first kit.

1/144 scale high grades (HG) are cheap and affordable. As for complextiy Wing Zero or Wing Gundam is always a fun kit to start off with.

A lot of those kits on the page your link goes to appear to be very old, they are easy to build, due to maybe 40+ parts, but the detail and range of movement is sparse compared to the recent HG 1/144 kits from build fighters, Unicorn/Universal Century era, and the thunderbolt kits are all recent. Real Grade are like mini master grades, some cost around the same as certain high grade kits (like Full Armor Destroy Mode Unicorn), but a little more detail, and some self adhesive clear decals. Master grade (MG) are a little more in both size, complexity, and cost. Perfect Grade (PG) are the largest, and easily the most expensive kits you could buy, on your current budget you could get one in a couple of years (I'm not even interested in getting them).

In terms of tools, I use side cutters from the hobby store bought mine for $8 US dollars, and a hobby knife (you can buy Xacto clones for a few dollars less than what they want), a rounded file, and a flat file (bought mine from Games Workshop years ago, occasional clean with rubbing alcohol brings the life back to the file, and removes the stuff stuck in the surface), and some fine grit sand paper. I hardly use the knife set, the side cutter does a good job of getting the part off the sprue, and then I file off the nubs, and that's it.

I'd start with an HG kit if you haven't built any models before, just take your time, read the diagram a few times, if it doesn't make any sense I go here to get it translated.

Definitely 1/144, but I'd recommend something newer. The one I started with was the MSZ 008 Zeta 2, that might be your style. I'd also recommend checking out the High-Grade Build Fighters (HGBF) line, they encompass a lot of different model types, and could show you which types you like best.
